annotations.text:
Eight storefront templates for VYA sellers.

Each one is a full homepage at 1200px, built from section types that already exist in storefront-blocks.ts. They differ on STRUCTURE first — grid density runs 2-up to 5-up, section count runs 6 to 10 — with palette and type following that, not leading it.

Top row: Heirloom, Provenance, The Index, Drop.
Bottom row: Dear Reader, Sugar, Vitrine, Corner Shop.

On the copy: this is DEFAULT text a template ships with — plain, concrete, and light to edit. No invented shop names, founders, cities or inventory, and no jokes or moralising at the shopper. It says what the thing is.

Anything only the seller can supply is bracketed and shows through as a placeholder: YOUR STORE, [YOUR NAME], [YOUR EMAIL], [YOUR STREET ADDRESS], [AMOUNT], [DROP DATE], [Customer name]. Prices read $0.00 until real inventory fills them.

Voice still differs between templates, but through register and typography rather than personality: Heirloom is formal, Dear Reader is first person, Sugar is lowercase, Vitrine says as little as it can.

Each template turns on one structural move, and no two heroes are composed the same way:

Heirloom — type-first hero on paper, image band below; philosophy statements interrupt the grid
Provenance — hero text bottom-RIGHT over a proof strip; label wall AND era timeline
The Index — search bar IS the hero, centred, no full-bleed photo
Drop — countdown above everything, then a giant centred poster and a three-image strip
Dear Reader — image LEFT, text RIGHT; a real letter at reading width
Sugar — a card overlapping the photo, rotated badge; categories named by feeling
Vitrine — one line dead centre; 2-up grid at 80px gutters
Corner Shop — diptych with a centred band; address and hours above the first product
